summary: Performance is adequate for this app's scale (tens of sites per month, single desktop user) and meaningfully better than the prior audit assumed. The two scariest hot-path risks are mitigated: startup recovery is fully deferred (3000ms) and async so it never blocks the UI (main.ts:224-234), and the overview list-build avoids per-row approval N+1 by opting out of approval resolution and pre-loading latestApprovals/hidden rows as single batch queries (performance-management-service.ts:683-712). The toDetail N+1 (one approval query per entry) is still latent and only avoided because the hot caller passes resolveEntryApprovalStatus:false — any default-option caller pays it. verification.reasoning: Read schedule-return-performance-parser.ts at the cited ranges in current 0.4.30 source (package.json version confirmed 0.4.30). resolveVirtualScheduleItemFromHolidayTable (lines 725-766) is defined as claimed: it loops over input.layout.rescheduleDateCells (skipping rows whose date != input.workDate via continue), then nests over supportedWorkingDutyCodes and slot columns, reading regularName/changedName from worksheet cells via normalizeCellText. The function then unconditionally returns { foundNoneMarker: false, scheduleItem: null } (lines 762-765). I verified the helpers it calls (normalizeDateText, normalizeCellText, isVirtualOriginalWorker, isNoneActualWorker, normalizeLookupKey) are pure read/normalize functions with no mutation, no logging, no accumulator — so the entire nested iteration is genuinely side-effect-free dead work. The call site (lines 1272-1280) invokes it, but only on a narrow path: !directScheduleItem && isVirtualOriginalWorker(originalWorker) where the virtual marker is the literal placeholder name "홍길동" (line 130). I traced every downstream use of its return value: line 1296 (!virtualScheduleItem?.foundNoneMarker → always !false=true), line 1308 (virtualScheduleItem?.scheduleItem in the scheduleItem ?? chain → always null, never contributes), line 1319 (!virtualScheduleItem?.scheduleItem → always true), and lines 1362-1363 (signature always records false/null). So the result is fully constant and the path simply falls through to slotScheduleItem. This is the same dead resolver as prior-audit finding #6, STILL-OPEN in 0.4.30 (last touch to this file was 455f4a8, an unrelated holiday slot-time fallback fix; the dead resolver was not removed). One minor over-statement: it is NOT invoked per substitute row but only per qualifying row (virtual original worker + no direct schedule item), so the wasted-iteration cost is narrower than "per qualifying substitute row" implies — but the qualification "per qualifying substitute row" is itself technically correct. Severity low is the right calibration: it is dead/wasteful code, not a payroll-correctness defect — a null result yields a warning alert and falls through to the slot-time path rather than producing wrong pay.

The v0.4.30 CI run is stuck 'queued' (gh run list shows queued ~1h with no completion) while gh release view shows v0.4.30 was published (draft:false) at 2026-06-14T09:37:15Z. CI is not a required status check, not wired to publish, and currently executes nothing — so it provides no actual gate on production.

verification.finding: CI exists but is non-blocking theater — release shipped while CI never ran (0.4.30 process gate)
verification.reasoning: Traced every claim to source and live GitHub state; all hold for current 0.4.30. (1) ci.yml is NEW since 0.4.29: absent from release/0.4.29 (empty ls-tree), present on release/0.4.30 via commit 8b855ed "chore(ci): add self-hosted CI workflow", later patched by e45e6fd to guard Windows path tests. So prior finding #3 ("ZERO automated tests, no CI") is now PARTIAL — a CI file exists. (2) The job targets a runner that does not exist: .github/workflows/ci.yml:22 runs-on [self-hosted, Linux, X64], and the runners API returns total_count:0, runners:[] — nothing can ever pick the job up. (3) The single CI run for v0.4.30 (id 27494809260, event push, branch release/0.4.30) is status=queued / conclusion=empty, created 2026-06-14T09:35:32Z, still queued ~1h6m later; it is the ONLY run that has ever existed for this workflow and there are zero completed runs in repo history. (4) Meanwhile gh release view v0.4.30 shows isDraft:false, publishedAt 2026-06-14T09:37:15Z — the release went public ~2 minutes after CI was queued, with CI never running. (5) CI is not wired as a gate: branch protection on both main and release/0.4.30 returns 404 "Branch not protected" (no required status checks), and package.json release:publish = build && release:check && electron-builder --publish always && publish-release-assets.mjs — it never runs npm test; release-check.mjs only validates required files/.env keys/RELEASE_MANIFEST.json, not tests. So the publish path is fully decoupled from CI. The defect is real and still present. If anything it is mildly understated (not one CI run has ever completed in repo history, so the gate value is exactly zero, not merely weak), but high is appropriate: it is the same uncontrolled-publish risk as prior high finding #3, now with a non-functional CI facade rather than a true regression.

criticalFindings.title: No merge/PR/review discipline; releases cut from live working branch; main abandoned
criticalFindings.detail: Repo has zero pull requests and zero merge commits. main is 26 commits behind at 0.4.24 and never receives the active line. v0.4.30's tag, its release/0.4.30 branch, and the working feature branch feature/perf-recovery-cleanup-A all resolve to the same commit d08080f, meaning the release was published directly from the in-progress working branch with no review or stabilization boundary. No human-review evidence exists for any shipped payroll change.
criticalFindings.evidence: git log --merges (empty); gh pr list --state all (empty); git rev-list --count main..HEAD = 26; git rev-parse HEAD v0.4.30 release/0.4.30 all = d08080f6...; main last commit dd6cdea (0.4.24)

verification.finding: No merge/PR/review discipline; releases cut from live working branch; main abandoned at 0.4.24
verification.reasoning:
I independently reproduced every cited fact against the live repo at the released commit. (1) Zero merge commits: `git log --merges` returns nothing (count 0). (2) Zero PRs: `gh pr list --state all` and `gh api repos/hacker943410-debug/ShiftMS/pulls?state=all` both return `[]` with a valid authenticated token (gh auth status = logged in, repo scope), so the empty result is real, not an auth artifact. (3) Convergence: HEAD, tag v0.4.30, branch release/0.4.30, and working branch feature/perf-recovery-cleanup-A ALL resolve to d08080f6ed3b7f25267533bc28265dee590d6be5; `git rev-list --left-right --count release/0.4.30...feature/perf-recovery-cleanup-A` = 0/0 (byte-identical). So v0.4.30 was tagged on the exact tip of the in-progress working branch — no stabilization or review boundary between "working" and "released." (4) main abandonment: `git rev-list --count main..HEAD` = 26 (finding said 26), `HEAD..main` = 0, and main's tip is dd6cdea = "릴리즈.0.4.24.게시결과" both locally and on origin. The active 0.4.25–0.4.30 line never merges back to main. The shipped release commit d08080f only bumps package.json version + adds release docs; all payroll logic changes (auto-archive holiday gate, hand-moved-orphan recovery, atomic mark-effective) landed on this same unreviewed branch (2abe9cf, 45ac52a, cbdde71, 455f4a8, 29da715). 

Two nuances refine but do not overturn the finding: (a) A CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml (typecheck + npm test + build) now EXISTS and is committed at d08080f — so the repo is no longer entirely gate-less on paper. However it triggers on `push` (branches '**') and pull_request, NOT as a pre-release/merge gate, and it requires `runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64]`. The repo has ZERO self-hosted runners registered (actions/runners total_count=0), so the single triggered run (id 27494809260, branch release/0.4.30, event=push) has been stuck `status: queued` for over an hour and can never complete. It therefore provided no actual gate for v0.4.30, which was already cut and tagged before any CI could pass. (b) The finding says all three refs "resolve to d08080f" implying the release was published from the working branch; precisely, only release/0.4.30 (identical commit) was pushed to origin — feature/perf-recovery-cleanup-A is local-only and not on origin — but since they are the same commit this is a distinction without a difference. Severity stays HIGH (not critical): the gap is real and unmitigated for a payroll app, but it is a process/quality-assurance weakness rather than a demonstrated incorrect-payment defect; the directly money-affecting risks are tracked under other findings.

criticalFindings.title: Manual QA/sign-off artifacts regressed for 0.4.30
criticalFindings.detail: Earlier releases carried structured QA artifacts (e.g. v0.4.29 has QA_CHECKLIST.md, RESULT_REPORT.md, IMPLEMENTATION_ANALYSIS.md, and a logs/ dir). v0.4.30's artifacts/releases/v0.4.30/ contains only RELEASE_MANIFEST.json and an empty logs/ directory — no sign-off log, no QA checklist. Combined with no test gate and a non-running CI, 0.4.30 shipped with the weakest verification trail of the recent line.
criticalFindings.evidence: ls artifacts/releases/v0.4.30/ -> RELEASE_MANIFEST.json only; logs/ empty; vs artifacts/releases/v0.4.29/ -> QA_CHECKLIST.md, RESULT_REPORT.md, logs, screenshots

verification.finding: Manual QA/sign-off artifacts regressed for 0.4.30
verification.reasoning:
The core factual claim is REAL and STILL PRESENT in 0.4.30, but the severity is overstated and the supporting evidence is partly inaccurate.

CONFIRMED facts (traced in source):
- A documented standard artifact set exists in TWO places: artifacts/releases/README.md "표준 구조" and docs/patch-workflow.md "버전 폴더 표준 구조" (lines ~37-50). Both list 11 entries: README.md, COMPACT_CONTEXT.md, IMPLEMENTATION_ANALYSIS.md, FILE_IMPACT.md, FUNCTIONAL_SPEC.md, RELEASE_MANIFEST.json, TODO.md, QA_CHECKLIST.md, RESULT_REPORT.md, logs/, screenshots/.
- v0.4.30 contains ONLY RELEASE_MANIFEST.json. `git ls-files artifacts/releases/v0.4.30/` returns just that one file. No QA_CHECKLIST.md, no RESULT_REPORT.md, no IMPLEMENTATION_ANALYSIS.md, no logs/, no screenshots/.
- This IS a regression vs the preceding line: v0.4.25, v0.4.26, v0.4.27, v0.4.28, and v0.4.29 ALL carried the full 11-entry set. So 0.4.30 is the weakest documentation trail of the recent line, matching only the older v0.4.24 (which also had just README + manifest).
- The release WAS shipped: package.json version=0.4.30, tag commit d08080f "릴리즈.0.4.30...", manifest publishedAt 2026-06-14T09:00:00Z. The 0.4.30 diff touched approval/auto-archive/orphan-recovery logic (commits 2abe9cf, a9c75e1, 455f4a8, etc.), so shipping with no QA_CHECKLIST/RESULT_REPORT record is a real process gap for payroll-affecting changes.

CORRECTIONS / OVERSTATEMENTS in the claim:
- The claim's evidence implies v0.4.29 had populated "logs, screenshots." FALSE: v0.4.29's logs/ and screenshots/ dirs are EMPTY, and its QA_CHECKLIST.md (11 checkbox lines) / RESULT_REPORT.md are short markdown stubs. The prior "verification trail" was already thin — checklists, not captured evidence. So the delta to 0.4.30 is smaller than the claim implies.
- The claim says v0.4.30 "logs/ empty." Slightly wrong: v0.4.30 has NO logs/ directory at all, not an empty one.
- The claim couples this to "no test gate and a non-running CI." Overstated: a self-hosted CI workflow was added (commits 8b855ed, e45e6fd) and scripts/release-signoff.mjs runs typecheck+test+package+packaged-smoke+installer-smoke+audit. These are real, though not wired into release:publish.

WHY LOW, NOT MEDIUM: The missing items are manually-authored markdown / empty placeholder dirs that were NEVER an enforced gate. scripts/validate-structure.mjs validates only unrelated agent-scaffolding files, not the release artifact set; scripts/release-check.mjs validates only RELEASE_MANIFEST.json shape + a fixed build-output file list. Nothing in the toolchain enforces QA_CHECKLIST/RESULT_REPORT, so their absence cannot block or corrupt a build. The ONE artifact that is functionally load-bearing for production — RELEASE_MANIFEST.json, which drives auto-update (latest.yml) and in-app patch notes — IS present and passes release:check. No pay math, approval history, or data integrity is affected by the missing markdown. The genuine underlying risk (a payroll release with no recorded QA sign-off) is a restatement of the pre-existing "release:publish runs zero tests / no quality gate" finding (prior finding #3), not a new defect created by these missing files. As a process/documentation-trail issue with zero runtime or correctness impact, this is low.

criticalFindings.title: Auto-update packages remain unsigned
criticalFindings.detail: Windows build sets signAndEditExecutable:false and there is no certificate/CSC configuration; electron-updater serves latest.yml from public GitHub releases. Unsigned auto-updates for a payroll desktop app are a supply-chain/tamper risk on the delivery path.
criticalFindings.evidence: package.json:149 (signAndEditExecutable:false), no csc/certificate keys in build; src/main/services/app-update-service.ts:4,207 (electron-updater autoUpdater used)

verification.finding: Auto-update packages remain unsigned (Windows build disables signing via signAndEditExecutable:false with no CSC/certificate config; electron-updater serves latest.yml + NSIS installer from public GitHub releases).
verification.reasoning: Traced the full build-and-delivery path in 0.4.30. (1) package.json build config is the sole source of electron-builder config — no electron-builder.yml/yaml/json exists (Glob returned none), so everything is in package.json. (2) In the win block, package.json:149 sets "signAndEditExecutable": false. A targeted grep across all json/mjs/cjs/js/yml/nsh/ps1 files for every signing key (CSC_LINK, WIN_CSC, certificateFile, certificateSubjectName, verifyUpdateCodeSignature, publisherName, signAndEditExecutable, forceCodeSigning) returned exactly ONE hit: package.json:149. So there is no certificate, no CSC env path, and no signature-verification setting anywhere. (3) .env.example contains no signing vars. (4) The afterPack hook build/after-pack-set-icon.cjs contains no sign/csc/certificate logic (grep over build/** returned no matches) — it only sets the icon. (5) package.json:88-95 sets publish provider github (owner hacker943410-debug, repo ShiftMS, releaseType draft), so electron-builder emits latest.yml and the installer is distributed from public GitHub releases. (6) app-update-service.ts:4 imports autoUpdater from electron-updater and :207 uses it (updater = dependencies.updater ?? autoUpdater); the service wires checkForUpdates (:360), downloadUpdate (:438) and quitAndInstall (:478). Net: the delivered NSIS installer and the auto-update payload are unsigned, and electron-updater on NSIS does not enforce code-signature verification without a publisher/certificate, so a tampered release asset would be accepted. The defect is REAL and STILL PRESENT. Severity: the auditor's "medium" is correct, not critical — transport is HTTPS via GitHub and release-asset integrity depends on GitHub account security, so the practical attack surface is narrower than a generic supply-chain claim; it remains a legitimate tamper/hardening gap on the delivery path for a payroll app. Minor wording note: signAndEditExecutable:false is an additional disable of rcedit/signing, but even without it the absence of any CSC config already yields unsigned artifacts — the conclusion is unchanged.
